newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo says interested in Unilever units.
newsitem.headline: Akzo says interested in Unilever units.

text.p: Chemicals group Akzo Nobel NV said on Thursday it was looking with interest at the chemicals businesses recently put up for sale by Unilever.
"We have requested an insight into the documents with the bank handling the transaction," Akzo chairman Cornelis van Lede said at a results news conference.
Of the four Unilever units up for sale Unichema International and Crosfield were the most interesting Van Lede added.
He said the activities of Unilever's Quest unit were not of interest to Akzo, while parts of National Starch might prove interesting.
Dutch biochemicals and food group Gist Brocades on Wednesday it was interested in a possible acquisition of the Quest flavours and fragrances unit.
Unilever said earlier in February that the businesses it planned to sell off had combined turnover, including sales to other Unilever companies, of three billion stg in 1996.
National Starch and Chemical Co is a worldwide producer of industrial adhesives, resins and speciality chemicals, headquartered in the United States.

Unichema is based in the Netherlands and is involved in speciality oleochemicals and nickel catalysts, while Crosfield, a producer of inorganic chemicals based on silica and alumina, is headquartered in Britain.
